Synopsis:
Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim reinstates subsidised fuel purchase quotas (RON95 petrol to 300L/month, diesel to 400L/month per eligible user), reversing earlier cuts made during the U.S.-Israel-Iran war-driven crude price spike. The package also includes education funding, digital health, SME micro-financing, and AI access for youth. The move is politically motivated ahead of a potential snap election, with Anwar's coalition facing declining support after losing three successive regional elections.
